title: Volumetric Decontamination of Raw Meat and Surfaces Using Bacteriophage Microaerosols
content: Foodborne pathogens such as Salmonella enterica serovar Typhimurium pose persistent risks in meat-processing environments, often evading conventional chemical sanitizers. This study evaluates the efficacy of bacteriophage microaerosols for volumetric decontamination of raw meat and food-contact surfaces. A lytic phage cocktail (109 PFU/mL) was nebulized into a sealed chamber (0.4 m3) containing inoculated chicken breast meat, glass, and stainless-steel substrates. Complete elimination of S. Typhimurium was achieved after 1 hour exposure with 3 mL of phage suspension, yielding ≥5-log10 reductions across all surfaces. The aerosolized phages retained infectivity and distributed uniformly, outperforming traditional surface-spray methods. These findings support bacteriophage microaerosols as a residue-free, eco-compatible alternative for food-safety applications, with potential for industrial-scale deployment.
